title: Spaghetti al Pomodoro

overview.description: Spaghetti tossed with a simple, slowly simmered tomato sauce made with tomatoes, garlic, olive oil and basil.

ingredients: 50g finely grated Parmesan or Pecorino, optional
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over low heat.
Add the sliced garlic and cook gently until fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomatoes and crush them with a wooden spoon.
Season lightly with salt and black pepper.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered for 30–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and the flavour has deepened.
Tear most of the basil leaves and stir them into the sauce near the end of cooking.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente according to the packet instructions.
Reserve a mugful of the pasta cooking water.
Add the spaghetti to the tomato sauce.
Toss thoroughly, adding a little pasta water if necessary to loosen the sauce.
Serve with the remaining basil and grated cheese if using.

learning.did-you-know: Pomodoro means 'tomato' in Italian. Spaghetti al pomodoro is a classic example of Italian cooking where a small number of simple ingredients are used to create a complete dish.
learning.what-you-will-learn: How slowly cooking tomatoes develops flavour and how pasta cooking water can help a sauce cling to the pasta.

notes.why-its-in-the-chapman-kitchen: A simple, affordable and family-friendly pasta dish that is useful as both a complete meal and a foundation for more elaborate pasta recipes.
chapman-tips: Use good-quality tinned tomatoes if possible.
Don't brown the garlic heavily or it can make the sauce bitter.
A gentle simmer gives the tomatoes time to become sweeter and more concentrated.
The starch in the reserved pasta water helps the sauce emulsify and cling to the pasta.
Add the pasta to the sauce rather than simply pouring sauce over the pasta.
The sauce can be made in a larger batch and frozen separately.
notes.batch-cooking: Freezes well. The tomato sauce freezes particularly well and can be made in a large batch. Cooked spaghetti can also be frozen, although freshly cooked pasta gives the best texture.
notes.leftovers: Leftover spaghetti can be reheated gently or used to make a frittata di spaghetti.
